name: Gore-Tex lip implant (SoftForm)

lead: Gore-Tex lip implants are thin strips or tubes of expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) that a surgeon places in the lip to add permanent volume. Wikipedia lists SoftForm, Advanta and UltraSoft as commercial versions, in diameters of 1.6 mm or 4.8 mm.
The material is a long-established surgical implant in vascular and facial plastic surgery. No clinical studies specific to lip use were found in the sources reviewed, so this entry is short.

paras: The implant is a solid or hollow ePTFE tube inserted into the lip tissue, where it physically occupies space and so increases lip volume.

Wikipedia lists implant movement and extrusion (breaking through the tissue) among complications of lip implants, along with bleeding, asymmetry and lumpiness. Unlike hyaluronic acid fillers, an implant is a physical device rather than an injectable.

lead: Gore-Tex lip implants are strips or tubes of expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) used for lip augmentation. Wikipedia describes them as 1.6 mm or 4.8 mm in diameter and names Advanta, UltraSoft and SoftForm as commercial versions [1].

ePTFE is also used as a graft and implant material in vascular, cardiac, hernia and facial plastic surgery [2]. For lips specifically, the sources reviewed provide little beyond a description and a list of complications, and no clinical studies were found.
infobox: Strips or tubes, 1.6 mm or 4.8 mm diameter [1]

paras: Lip implants made of Gore-Tex are delivered as strips or tubes and sold under names including SoftForm [1]. Wikipedia presents them among several lip augmentation options that also include fillers, fat transfer, donor tissue and surgical flaps [1].

Wikipedia lists implant-specific complications of lip augmentation as movement of the implant and extrusion through the tissue, and more general ones including bleeding, uneven lips and lumpiness [1].
